The brazier catches. Blue fire, cold to look at, warm to stand by. The frost on the nearest courtier starts to run.
The brazier burns.
The second brazier catches. A frozen courtier's eyes move, very slowly, toward the light.
The brazier burns.
The third brazier catches. Ice drips from the portcullis like a thaw in spring.
The brazier burns.
The portcullis of black ice melts through and falls in a shower of water.
...Warm. Is it spring? It was going to be spring. His Majesty said it would be spring. We waited in the hall.
It is not spring, Lady Esk. I am sorry. It will be, soon. I promise it will be something.
I carry messages up the stair. Nobody reads them. They say 'the court asks to be excused.' Every one says that.
You hold the brazier's flame to the postern's seal. It thaws, and the door to the Stair Head opens.
The postern stands open.
The under-court's hall is full of one enormous mourner: a body made of courtiers, bowed under a hood of frost.
We grieve. We grieve. We were told to wait. We were told it would be spring.
...Majesty. You came down. Is it spring?
No. It is the end of winter. That is the best I can do. Come out of the cold.
(When bells toll once for each of you, a procession is coming. Fire and light melt it; cure doom.)
The Mourning Court comes apart into courtiers, one by one, and each of them sits down on the floor as if very tired.
The under-throne. A small crown lies frozen to its seat, the kind a regent wears when the king is away.
The Mourning Court fills the hall.
My court. I kept you because I could not bear an empty hall. That was my grief, not yours.
You may go. All of you. Rest, or walk up into the thaw, or go to Cenotaph and be honoured. I release you.
The courtiers get up, stiffly. Some lie down again, content. Some start up the stair. Lady Esk curtseys before she goes.
And the crown. Mine outlived my people by three hundred years. It should not outlive the reason I wore it.

options.text: "Carry it until the Ashen Crown is broken."

cmds.text: The Lich King lifts off his crown of rime and sets it on the under-throne beside the regent's. It looks smaller there. So does he, and he seems glad.
There. An emperor of nobody. It is very restful.
Then I will carry it a little longer, as a reminder, and set it down the day the last crown breaks.
It is heavy. Good. It ought to be.
(The Lich King received Dawn Conductor.)
The under-throne is empty now, except for what was left on it on purpose.
The Crypt-Gate. The door between the fault's crypts and the Hollow Throne. I held it once, with the dead.
When I left, my first student stayed to hold it. Sorrow. She was very young. She is not young any more.
I owe her an apology. She is going to want more than that.
QC15: Descend Velkhar's Crypt-Gate and find Sorrow, his first student.
Velkhar's Crypt-Gate: find Sorrow at the gate.
The pull-chain rattles through the niches. The bone lattice lifts out of the lane.
The lattice is up.
'HALDIS, BAKER. HELD THE WEST DOOR FOUR NIGHTS. RELEASED WITH THANKS.' The tag is newer than the rest. Someone has re-tied it.
Haldis. She kept telling the others to stop moaning. I thanked every one of them. I'm glad I did that part right.
We hold the doors. Lord Velkhar asked. Then he left, and Sorrow asked. We don't know how to stop being asked.
Strangers. We hold these doors. Something below wants out. Will you hold them after we let go? Promise it.
Then we hold.
...My lord. You came back. We held. We held the whole time.
I know. Thank you. You can let go now. I will see to what's below.
The dead at the doors lower their arms, all together, the way you set down something you have carried too long.
The doors are yours to hold now. They don't weigh as much as you'd think. They weigh exactly as much as you'd think.
The chain falls away from the charnel door. The Crypt Road is just beyond.
The door is open.
Before the Crypt-Gate stands a woman in grey, older than the gate looks. The dead around her stand at attention.
Another lot, come to open my gate. I held it. Every night since he left. I will hold it against you.
...You. You came back. A hundred years late and dressed for travel.
Sorrow. I'm sorry.
He taught you too? Then he taught you wrong. Let me show you what I learned alone.
(When the crypt-gate grinds closed behind you, she is shutting you in. Light hurts her; cure blind.)
Sorrow lowers her hands. The dead around her sit down on the steps of the gate, and so does she.
He left. I stayed. Someone had to. That's the whole story. It's a short one for a hundred years.
You laid them to rest and left. Do you know where they went? They didn't rest. She took them.
Who?
Your teacher. Mine too, before you. Mother Sepulchre. Every soul you put down, she picked up and adopted into her Court.
I held this gate so she couldn't have the rest. Go and get them back, if you want to say sorry properly.
...And you?
I'll sit down. I haven't sat down in a hundred years. Go.
QC15: Mother Sepulchre, Velkhar's teacher, has adopted the dead he laid to rest. Go to Sepulchre Court.
Sepulchre Court: confront Mother Sepulchre.
I'm sitting down. It's wonderful. Tell him that. Don't tell him I said it was wonderful.
Below the Hollow Throne, below the dead, there is a heart. It beats slowly. Each beat is a page turning.
Every account the Crown ever kept, of everything it took and everything it gave back, is kept down here.
I can feel the fragment of something here. Not a dragon. Something the Crown made out of what it took.
I came to find my page. Everyone has a page down here. I found the door to the first keeper and stopped.
Three keepers, three doors. Behind the last, the crown that was never worn. I'm going back up. You should too. You won't.
The keeper's door is sealed. The Ledger is not ready for you.
The door opens onto a room of ledgers that reach the dark. The Ledger looks up.
The keeper's books close. Somewhere deeper, a lock turns.
You back out. The counting resumes behind the door.
The keeper's room is quiet. The books are closed.
The keeper's door is sealed. The Tally is not ready for you.
The door opens onto a room of ledgers that reach the dark. The Tally looks up.
The keeper's books close. Somewhere deeper, a lock turns.
You back out. The counting resumes behind the door.
The keeper's room is quiet. The books are closed.
The keeper's door is sealed. The Verdict is not ready for you.
The door opens onto a room of ledgers that reach the dark. The Verdict looks up.
The keeper's books close. Somewhere deeper, a lock turns.
You back out. The counting resumes behind the door.
The keeper's room is quiet. The books are closed.
The innermost door. Behind it, something the size of a crown and the weight of a kingdom turns, slowly, looking for a head.
The door is sealed three times over, once for each keeper, and once more for the four wyrms. It will not open yet.
The door opens. The Unmade Crown turns toward you and, for the first time, finds a head it likes.
Raven. Whatever happens in there, it does not get to be worn.
The crown that was never made comes apart into the thing it always was: ash, and a little light.
...There. Nobody wears it. Not ever.
You step back. The door stays open. It is patient. Crowns are.
The innermost room is empty but for a little ash, and the ash is only ash.
You heard it too. Last night. Under the sea, once, and wrong.
That was the Crown's bell. It went down with Veyr. I cast it, when I was an apprentice. I would know its voice anywhere.
It rang at the fault. It shouldn't ring again.
Bells don't ring themselves. Something down there is pulling the rope.
My diving bell still holds air. I'll lower you. I won't come down. I'm old, not stupid.
Ride Anse's diving bell down to drowned Veyr and find out what is ringing the Crown's bell.

options.text: Go down in the diving bell

cmds.text: The sea isn't going anywhere. Neither am I.
The diving bell sinks through green, then grey, then a dark that has weight.
It's quiet down there now. I sleep better. So does the sea.
The keys are bell-ringers' keys, one for each tower of old Veyr. Someone has kept them polished.
Someone has been waiting for a visitor.
The empty bowl. The altar has nothing more to give.
The first bell speaks: low, round, patient. The water in the carillon trembles and settles.
The first bell hums, still answering.
The second bell answers the first. Somewhere above, a grille of bell-metal shifts.
The second bell swallows the note before it sounds. It will not speak first.
The second bell hums, still answering.
The cracked bell rings last, and right. Three notes hang in the water as one chord. The grille at the top of the stair folds open.
That is the note the Crown's bell was cast to ring. It has forgotten.
The cracked bell groans and falls silent. The others have not spoken yet.
The chord still hangs in the water.
A grille of bell-metal closes the stair. Three bells wait in the carillon below, each marked with its place in the order.
The belfry. The Crown's great bell hangs over nothing, from no rope. It swings anyway.
No one is pulling it.
It is pulling itself. It rang the fault into the world. It wants to ring it again, and get it right this time.
The bell turns its mouth toward the party.
The bell stops swinging. For the first time in a long time, the sea around Veyr is silent.
It rang its last note. The right one.

options.text: Leave the bell in the deep

cmds.text: Let it sleep where it fell.
Anse can hang it in the harbour. Somebody should ring it on purpose.
Ride the diving bell back up and tell Anse the sea is quiet.
The empty cradle. The water inside the ring does not move.
Later, in Hearthward, they tell it around the communal fire, and everyone tells it slightly wrong.
The Crown's bell hangs in the harbour now. Anse rings it at dawn, badly, and nobody asks him to stop.
The Crown's bell stays in the deep. On quiet nights the sailors say they can hear it not ringing.
Five names are carved on the lift housing at the Conduit, with the tenders' names beneath: everyone who came up at the last second.
The Bound still sit together some nights, around a green fire nobody else can see. Nobody asks them to explain. They are still five.
Far below, in the Hollow Heart, the Unmade Crown stays unmade. The crypts are quiet. The ledger is closed.
Is it finished?
No. It's started. That's what we get.
A courier in quarry dust pushes through the crowd on the quay, a letter held out in front of her like a torch.
From Mara at Brackenford. She said give it to the one with the dragon in him, and she said run.
'The quarry floor fell in on the fourth night. There are lights under it. Crown surveyors went down after them and the ones who came back won't say what they saw. Come home. - M.'
Raven. Under the quarry. I can feel them from here. Fragments. Old ones. Lots of them.
You never said there was anything under the quarry.
I never knew. They were asleep. Something has been digging.
Mara's letter: the Crown Quarry's floor has collapsed onto something below. Crown surveyors went down. Ilyr senses dragon fragments. Return to the quarry's Heartglass Face.
The Crown Quarry fell in on itself. There are lights down there, and the Crown already has men in the hole.
The quarry floor went on the fourth night. The Heartglass Face split right across. You go carefully, down there.
You've been below. I can smell it on you: hot stone and old bones. The Crown's still digging, isn't it.
The digging's stopped. The quarry's quiet at night again. First time in years. I don't know what you did. Thank you for it.
The Heartglass Face has split from roof to floor. Cold air pours out of the crack, and under the cold, a warmth like breath.
Here. It goes down, and down. The fragments are under us. Many. And men with picks among them.
The Crown's mining the dead.
Not the dead. Sleepers. They are digging sleepers out of their beds.
Survey stakes lead into the crack. Someone has already cut steps.
The Heartglass Face opens onto a collapse. Crown survey stakes lead down into the depths. Follow them to wherever the Crown is digging.
The shaft drops away into warm dark. Far below, something glows the colour of a banked forge.
That's the way. Whatever you do down there, don't let them wake the ones who can't be woken.
A Crown survey stake, driven into the rock. The tag reads DEEP LEVEL 1 - CLAIMED. Below it someone has scratched: 'claimed by who'.
You're not on the roster. Nobody gets below without a Crown warrant.
...Fine. You'll go anyway. Everyone does. The foreman's at the dig. He calls it overtime. It's been overtime for a month.
The digging's stopped. I can feel them settling. Some of them. Not all.
We'll come back for the rest.
You keep saying 'we'. I'm starting to believe it.
The Crown's dig in Emberdeep is shut down. The Deep stays open: Karag Dun, Emberwell and the dragon realm are reachable through the Crown Quarry and the Breach.
A waystone. The rune under your palm is warm, and the roads it knows open behind your eyes.
The sigil's thread of light pulls toward every stone you have touched.
The diving hull ticks under the pressure. Lamps show the sea floor a stone's throw in every direction.
The auger's cable hangs down the shaft from the Lanternwake, far above in the Aurora Pit. A winch-seat waits.

options.text: Ride the winch up to the ship

cmds.text: The ground splits. Heat pours out of the crack, and then a head the size of a house.
Cindermaw, the Surface Wyrm, has been waiting under the Reach since before there was a Crown.
Cindermaw sinks back into the rock it came from. The cinders around it go out one by one.
The water heaves. Something longer than the ship rolls under it, and the sea goes dark with scales.
Thalassar, the Sea Wyrm. It rises to see what dared its coast.
Thalassar sinks without a ripple. Far below, something in the Abyssal Cradle stirs and is still.
The wind drops. The clouds ahead fold open like a hand, and a white wyrm comes out of them at the ship.
Aerith-Vael, the Sky Wyrm. The lanes have been its own since the first ships learned to fly.
Aerith-Vael falls away through the cloud, its long body turning slow as a feather. The wind comes back.
The cavern floor is breathing. The bones on it are not bones; they are a spine, and it is getting up.
Ossathrax, the Deep Wyrm. The Hollow Throne's dead step out of its way.
Ossathrax folds back into the dark. The dead come back to their places, as if nothing had walked there.
The Crucible Isle. A spar of rock in the sky, and on it the loudest building in the world.
Fighters to the hall, sightseers to the rail. Nobody jumps. We had one jump last year and he's still falling.
The cable winch is still here. The cable is not. It snapped in the fault, and the end of it hangs down into the cloud.
A flat of scored rock with mooring rings. Airships used to land here, when the owners could still afford them.
Cable's the only way up, and the cable goes back down to the Ninefold Shrine. Mind the gap when the basket swings.
The cable's gone. The fighters who were up here when the sky broke never left. Airships are the only road now.
Rank's chalked, odds are slated, the Bookmaker's in a good mood. Which means someone is about to lose a great deal.
Varro's at the top. He always is. Twenty-two years unbeaten. They say he's never been hit. They're wrong; he's just never fallen.
I ran supplies up here before the fault. I still do. Fighters don't stop wanting to fight because the world ended.
The ladder. Ten ranks, one at a time, no skipping. Win a rank and it pays, once. Lose and your rank stands.
Put something on the table and the house puts up something better. Win it, or leave it with me.
Solo bouts. One fighter, no friends, no excuses. Pick the fight, then pick who goes in.
Beast bouts. Your captured monster against one of ours. You watch; you don't fight. The stake's on the board.
The champion's gauntlet. Five fights in a row, no rest, no retreat. At the end of it, Varro.
Twenty-two years. I stopped counting the fights and started counting the fighters who came back. Keep the gate. I'm tired.
Rake the sand, wash the rail, mark the lines. The blood doesn't come out of the sand. We just turn it over.
I bet a month's wage on the Brass Pair and lost it on the second exchange. Worth it. Did you see the second exchange?
The crowd's half fighters and half people who couldn't get down after the cable snapped. Both halves cheer.
The world broke and they kept the ladder going. I don't know if that's brave or mad. I come every day.
The rope goes taut in your hand. Somewhere inside, under the water, a bell rings once. Nobody answers it.
I ring the hours. Low tide, high tide. There is no tide down here, but the town listens for the bell.
When Bellharbor sank we kept the air bell and the bell rope. Everything else we let the sea have.
Customs. Declare any goods brought from the surface. Nobody has declared anything in a year. I still ask.
I dive the Wreck of the Tithe for the Crown's gold. The hold's chained from below. Something down there likes gold more than I do.
I keep the tide tables for a harbour on the sea floor. Someone has to be ready for when the sea gives it back.
East of here the floor drops away into the trench. The old leviathans went down there to die. One of them didn't.
Old Bellharbor's tidemaster says a living leviathan keeps the Abyssal Cradle, at the bottom of the trench.
I light the lamps of the old district every night. Down here it's always night. So I never stop.
This district is under emergency law. It has been since it sank. Nobody has repealed it, and nobody will.
The Oath Gate stays shut until the emergency ends. I don't know who would declare it over. They're all down here with me.
I carried the Crown's writs for six years. By the Crown's own form: the emergency is ended. Go home.
...That is the correct form. Nobody has used it in a century.
The Magistrate unpins the seal from his coat. Across the district, the lamps dim one by one, gently, like people going to sleep.
The Oath Gate will open now. Its warden will not know the emergency is over. It never listened to anyone.
The emergency is over. I am told I may rest. I am considering it.
The bars grind apart. The empty armour behind them draws its sword and speaks the oath of the district to nobody.
The armour kneels and does not rise. On the step where it stood lies a helm, polished for a century.
The Oath Gate is locked by emergency law. The armour behind it has not blinked in a hundred years.
The gate stands open. The district's lamps are dark and calm.
The customs seal on the clapper is still intact. Whatever was declared in the hold, it was never paid.
The bell rings once. Below, the chains on the hatch go slack - and something comes up through it.
The hatch hangs open. The hold is mostly sea, but a customs strongbox has been dragged up onto the deck.
The bell is silent again, and the hold is open.
A voice from the kneeling coral, older than the reef: What comes every day, takes everything, and gives it all back?
The keeper closes its mouth. Across the nave, the coral hand on the sanctum door slowly opens.
The keeper says nothing. The coral hand stays closed.
The keeper is quiet. The sanctum stands open.
The coral hand holds the door shut.
The great shell breathes in, and out. Before it, on the altar, a smaller shell breathes in time with you.
Behind the rib-gate the dark goes on a long way down. Something breathes in it, slow as the tide. The gate does not open.

entities.msg: The quarry gate is barred.

entities.text: CROWN QUARRY - Ministry of Relays. Lift yard: north-east. Pump handles restore the drains.
A lunch pail sits on the table. The shift is two hours late.

entities.locked_msg: Raven: The spur floods past here. We need someone who understands the pumps.

entities.msg: A service gate, latched from the loft side.

entities.text: Scratched on the drain wall: 'Cale's crew was here. The stone hums at night.'

entities.msg: A loaded ore cart, held by the rail brake.

entities.text: Gauge: both pumps must run together. One crew holds a handle; the other pulls.
LEFT: rail brake. RIGHT: lift gate. Never open the lift with a crew aboard.

entities.msg: The service gate to the gallery. A latch is on this side.

entities.text: A surveyor's note: 'Fossil organs show no response to stimulus.' Someone has underlined 'no' twice.

entities.locked_msg: The yard passage is sealed by the extractor's pressure door.
Elowen: That's our road you're about to trample. Talk first.

entities.text: Irrigation map: 'Ford sluice feeds the upper camp. Three Sluices feed the grove bridges.'
A plaque copies the mural across the channel: water leaves the hill at the RIGHT, turns through the LEFT field, and only then feeds the MIDDLE grove.

entities.locked_msg: Roots hang too low to pass. Water would lift them.

entities.text: From the lookout you see the whole grove - and a hollow elm in the south-west, open on its far side.
Dry Gallery door: an ANCHOR glyph. 'Opens to the low tone.'
Wet Gallery door: a WAVE glyph. 'Opens to the middle tone.'

entities.locked_msg: The anchor door is sealed. It answers to a bell.
The wave door is sealed. It answers to a bell.

entities.text: Contract, pre-kingdom: 'Shared-body accords by consent, with a separation rite available to either party.'
A relay diagram. Six relays marked; a seventh line runs off the page toward 'Crown Dais - secondary'. Someone has pasted over it.
Ministry standardisation order, stamped: 'Separation rite: discontinued. Hosts: infrastructure.'

entities.locked_msg: A lantern-glyph door. It answers to the high tone.

entities.text: A diver's slate: 'Hearth token left on the east shelf-island. Mind the old steps.'
Identical grey uniforms on every bunk. Under one pillow: a child's drawing of a boat.
A footlocker: regulation kit, and a pressed flower nobody issued.
A bunk card: 'Warden 3'. Scratched beside it: 'Tam'.
x
x
x
A standing order: 'Seals are keyed to warrant numbers. Names are not required.'
Guard roster: 'Night token in the post's back locker. Return by dawn.'

entities.locked_msg: Oni: Not until every cell is open. That was the agreement.

entities.text: Aqueduct plate: 'Conduit service - three relay stations. Lift power is fed separately. Never cut the lifts.'
Ration chit, pinned to a crate: 'Quartermaster's spare badge is in the cage by the east wall. Mind the loose bar on the west side.'

entities.locked_msg: Two synchronization relays still hold the bridge doors. Release the south relay and reroute the north lift.
The third relay still drives the dais door.

entities.text: The stone falls in waves. Shaking dust shows where the next fall will land.
A tally on a crate: 'Dock master keeps a spare glass in the locker past the east bollards.'

entities.locked_msg: A sealed alcove. Something inside is singing with no words. You'd need a phrase to be let in.

entities.text: The engine manual.
A notice: 'Lantern stations are staffed. Knock, don't shout.'
The original authorization.
A binding seal.
A binding seal.
A binding seal.
The seal safe.
Scratched by a clerk: 'River, Crown, Ledger. The order the city was built in.'
A figure under a blanket, perfectly still. Frost on its eyelashes. It is a carved statue - someone's memorial, not a sleeper.

entities.locked_msg: Ice seals the north door. The warmth channels (east) could thaw it.

entities.msg: Solid ice. The three heat braziers could melt it together.

entities.text: A child's scratch on the ice: 'the warm hiding place is where the light bends east.'
The beacon lamp brightens and the bell sounds together. Then the tide surges across the reef. Cross while the lamp is dark.
The return beacon. Keep it lit, or nobody finds the way back.

entities.locked_msg: The channel east is black. The second beacon's light doesn't reach it yet.

entities.text: The wreck library.
A purser's note: 'Valuables in the aft locker, starboard. Past the bent rib.'

entities.locked_msg: The trench bell won't answer without the passenger register.

entities.msg: Elowen's survivors are meant to rebuild this crossing. Not yet.

entities.text: A memorial stone. The quarry ledger's numbers have been chiselled off; names are being cut in their place, one at a time.
The quarry gate is sealed with poured stone. The underground stays shut.
Memorial stones. Some bear names; most still bear numbers.
Elowen's chalk on a stump: three crossings, three sluice levers. 'Lift each lever to raise its walkway. The current eats whichever route stays low.'
x

entities.locked_msg: The current is too strong while any crossing is down. Raise all three walkways.
A crew chief: 'Yard's Quill's business. And Quill says he's waiting for someone who can light a lamp without burning down the street.'

entities.text: The workshop bench.

entities.msg: Fallen rope-bales block the upper walkway. A winch hangs above them.
More fallen bales. There's a second winch.

entities.text: Pennants lift before each gust. Cross between them. Each ballast anchor steadies the mooring a little more.
Wreckage from a rescue basket.
The memorial: a long wall of names. Every one of them fell.
The Returners' Wall.
Canal sign, repainted: 'LOCK GATES RAISE CROSSINGS. OPEN ONE, THE WATER SHIFTS.'

entities.locked_msg: A clerk's door, bolted from inside. The registrar has the key - after the Accord.
A sealed service door. Behind it, a machine is reading orders to no one.

entities.text: The original ledgers.
The Command Ledger.

entities.locked_msg: A sealed stair to the deep cells. The sanctuary keeps it shut until the Accord is signed.

entities.text: Fallowmere Ranch. Milk, eggs and seed. Close the gates. The quarry dogs come down at night.

entities.msg: The farmhouse door. Agna keeps it shut; the boys' boots are still by it.
The barn. Hay to the rafters and a tally of debts chalked on the door.
The dovecote. It smells of feathers and old straw.

entities.text: A slag vent. Warm air rises from it day and night. The pigs sleep against it in winter.
Soot Paddock. Pigs, coneys, doves. Truffles weighed at the gate, not after.

entities.msg: Brann's house. The windows are black with soot on the inside, too.
The sty-barn. Something inside snores like a furnace.

entities.text: Gullbank Croft. Salt-grass milk, sea-wind wool. Mind the tide line.

entities.msg: Maude's croft house. Nets dry in the window; nobody has fished from this house in years.
The byre. The door is swollen with salt and does not open for strangers.

entities.text: Windbreak Fold. Wool, milk, message doves. Rope yourself on the cliff path.

entities.msg: Sefton's house. The shutters are tied down with rope against the wind.
The fold barn. The wind has worn the door boards smooth as bone.

entities.text: Brinewell Steading. Salt-fed pork, brine eggs. Water is sold by the cup.

entities.msg: Yara's house. A salt crust has grown up the door like frost.
The steading barn, built of salt blocks. It sweats in the afternoons.

entities.text: A small fox gate, red lacquer over grey wood. Rice and a coin are left at its foot every morning.
Maple Gate Farm. By leave of the Court. Foxes are guests here; treat them so.

entities.msg: Okuni's house. A paper charm is pasted across the door: do not disturb the sleeping.
The barn. Lantern smoke has stained the beams the colour of tea.

entities.text: Lazar Fields. Clean meat, clean eggs, inspected by the Board. No one from the wards past this sign.

entities.msg: Gideon's house. Lime-washed, door and all. It smells of vinegar.
The barn. A Board of Quarantine seal hangs on the latch, signed and resigned.

entities.text: Rimefold. Cattle that do not die of cold. Shut the gate or they will walk to the Ice Road.

entities.msg: Hild's longhouse. A cow skull is nailed above the door, horns waxed.
The byre. Warm breath fogs through the gaps in the planks.

entities.locked_msg: Holt: The inspection waits for no one, Captain. Talk to the crew first.
Mara: Not before the lift. People are down there.

entities.text: Brackenford Halt. Crown Quarry: north road. Veyr: south over the river.
Oath Square. Ministry of Relays. Crown Records below.
The Oath Statue: 'I shall carry the Crown's orders.' Someone has scratched 'whose?' beneath.

entities.locked_msg: Raven: The door's barred. We need a way out that isn't this one.
Aurex: The records first. All of them.

entities.text: A ledger page: 'Unit 4419, dragonborn, Crown Quarry lift crew. Status: expendable material.' The unit has a name written in pencil: Wren.
Transport orders, stamped by the Marshal's office: heartglass cargo routed 'via Rootward sluices to the northern road.'

entities.msg: Two guards hold the north corridor. Their chalk marks point to the bell alcove.
The guards moved to the south corridor, toward the echo.

entities.text: Maintenance note: 'Overflow valve behind the east barrels. Mind the step.'

entities.locked_msg: The canal door is sealed by the Bailiff's stamp.
A foreman: 'Spine's closed to visitors. Talk to Quill at the regulator shop.'

entities.text: The canteen wall: a tally of injuries in chalk, row after row. No official ledger records it.
A regulator on the bench: brass coils around a cup of red heartglass. Morwen goes very quiet looking at it.

entities.locked_msg: Golem: Wait. You don't walk into the Spine without someone who knows the lines.

entities.text: Boiler walk: vents fire in turn. Watch the puff, then cross.

entities.locked_msg: The regulator crown is still at full pressure.
The bridge to the regulator crown is retracted until the pressure is balanced.

entities.text: Valve plaque: 'Cold spares in the south-west hatch. Refill before the shift ends.'
The harbor bell post. The bell was removed 'pending inspection'.
A confiscation shelf. Tags: 'forged passage papers, dock 3.' One ledger is chained, the chain unlocked.
Sak, whispering: 'Watch where they stand. They never leave their posts.'
Ballast locks: each lock steadies one lane of the span. Both locked: the middle lane goes calm.
Wind cues: pennants lift before each gust. Cross between gusts, or lock the ballast and take the calm middle lane.
Pilots' board: 'Spare clock-token on the windward shelf, behind the niche. Put it back.'
The memorial: a long wall of names. Every one of them fell. There is no wall for anyone who came back.
The wind shrine. Ochre cloth, weighted with stones, all streaming east.
The listening pool. When it is quiet, you can hear several people remembering the same morning differently.

entities.locked_msg: The choir door will not open to a partial record.

entities.text: x
A caretaker's note: 'Keep the day-token with the children's shelves, by the south-east alcove.'

entities.locked_msg: The choir door will not open to a partial record.
Mara: 'Not yet - you can barely stand. Help at the hearth first.'

entities.text: A sign nailed to a post: 'BRACKENFORD BAKERY - BEST RYE ON THE RIVER'. The river is somewhere under the sea now.
Painted board: 'CINDERWAKE CANTEEN - SHIFT STEW'. Someone has added: 'still open (sort of)'.

entities.msg: A broken section of walkway. Planks are stacked by the cots.

entities.text: The deck log. Every entry is signed by two crew, not one.

entities.msg: The Ice Road has not frozen hard enough to cross.
The Ice Road has not frozen hard enough to cross.
The Ice Road has not frozen hard enough to cross.
The Ice Road has not frozen hard enough to cross.

The high road is closed until the cable is working.
The high road is closed until the cable is working.
A salt slide blocks the road up to the basin.
A salt slide blocks the road up to the basin.
A salt slide blocks the road up to the basin.

Skychain patrols close the mountain road.

The coast road into the Skyspine washed out in the storms.
Quarantine wardens bar the fen causeway into Mirewold.
Quarantine wardens bar the fen causeway into Mirewold.
A checkpoint on the east road. The party is wanted in Veyr.
A checkpoint on the east road. The party is wanted in Veyr.
A checkpoint on the east road. The party is wanted in Veyr.
The Crown Heart relay is surrounded by a pressure storm.
A winter island, far to the north. Nacre's listeners say its lantern never goes out.
A starless shoal. Harbor bells ring when you pass it.
The tunnel ends in black water that swallows the lantern light.
The tunnel ends in black water that swallows the lantern light.
